questions.question: The base BC of a triangle ABC is divided at D such that BD = half of DC. The area of triangle ABC is _________ times the area of triangle ADC.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Triangles sharing a **common vertex** have their areas in the direct ratio of their **bases**.

Given, BD = (1/2) × DC ⇒ DC = 2 × BD

Total base BC = BD + DC = BD + 2 × BD = 3 × BD

Therefore, the ratio of the area of **triangle ABC** to **triangle ADC** is:

Area(ABC) ÷ Area(ADC) = BC ÷ DC = (3 × BD) ÷ (2 × BD) = 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is (3)/(2) times.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In **triangle ABC**, the **base BC** is divided at D such that BD = (1/2) × DC.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79469b7a829e66cdd49f15d7b5434f5168310b6a34c98edeeae7390d7cf010a7.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the length of **BD** be x.

⇒ DC = 2x

⇒ BC = BD + DC = x + 2x = 3x

Let h be the perpendicular height from vertex A to the base BC.

⇒ Area of **triangle ABC** = (1/2) × BC × h = (1/2) × 3x × h

⇒ Area of **triangle ADC** = (1/2) × DC × h = (1/2) × 2x × h

Now, let us find the ratio of the area of triangle ABC to the area of triangle ADC:

⇒ Area(ABC) ÷ Area(ADC) = ((1/2) × 3x × h) ÷ ((1/2) × 2x × h)

⇒ Area(ABC) ÷ Area(ADC) = 3x ÷ 2x = 3/2

⇒ Area(ABC) = (3/2) × Area(ADC)

Thus, the area of triangle ABC is **(3/2) times** the area of triangle ADC.

Let us analyze why the other options are incorrect:

Option (1) is incorrect because a ratio of 3 would require the base BC to be 3 times DC, which is false since BC is 1.5 times DC.

Option (2) is incorrect because a ratio of 4 would require the base BC to be 4 times DC.

Option (3) is incorrect because a ratio of 2 would require the base BC to be 2 times DC.

**∴ The correct answer is (3)/(2) times.**

**__Additional Information__**

Triangles with a Common Vertex

When two or more triangles share a **common vertex** and have their bases on the same straight line, their perpendicular heights are equal. Consequently, the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of their bases.

Median of a Triangle

A **median** divides a triangle into two triangles of equal area because it bisects the base, making the ratio of the bases 1:1.

Area Ratio Theorem

For any triangle ABC with a point D on BC, the ratio of the areas of the two sub-triangles is given by Area(ABD) ÷ Area(ADC) = BD ÷ DC.</p

questions.question: The mean score of class A of 40 students in the mathematics test of 30 marks is 23. The mean score of class B of 45 students in the same test is 22. What is the ratio of the mean score of both the classes to that of class A?
questions.solution:

Mean of class A = 23

Mean of class B = 22

**Concept used:**

Mean = Sum of the terms/No. of terms

**Calculation:**

Total score of class A = 40 × 23

⇒ 920

Total score of class B = 45 × 22

⇒ 990

Total score both the classes = 1910

Mean score of two classes together = 1910/85

Ratio = 1910/85 : 23

⇒ 382/17 : 23

⇒ 382 : 391

**∴ The ratio of the mean score of both the classes to that of class A is 382 : 391**

Total distance = 200 km

**Concept used:**

__Relative Speed of 2 bodies__ 

Sum of their individual speeds if they are moving in the opposite direction 

Difference of their individual speeds if they are moving in the same direction.

**Calculation:**

We know the total distance is 200 Km

If both trains crossed each other at a distance of 110 km then one train covered 110 km and the other 90 km [110+90=200km]

So ratio of their speed = 110 : 90 = 11 : 9

**∴ The ratio of their speed is 11 : 9**

questions.question: A solid metallic cylinder of base radius 3 cm and height 5 cm is melted to form cones each of height 1 cm and base radius 1 mm. How many cones were formed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a solid is melted to form identical smaller objects, the number of objects is equal to the ratio of their volumes.

Number of cones (N) = Volume of Cylinder ÷ Volume of 1 Cone

⇒ N = (π × R² × H) ÷ (1/3 × π × r² × h)

Convert everything to cm (R = 3 cm, H = 5 cm, r = 0.1 cm, h = 1 cm):

⇒ N = 3 × (3² × 5) ÷ (0.1² × 1) = (3 × 45) ÷ 0.01 = 135 ÷ 0.01 = 13,500

**∴ The correct answer is 13,500 cones.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89ea2695792746b73ea287d1a983ed4261caa969028065df9989100da384d4ce.png] 

**Given:**

For the cylinder:

⇒ Radius (R) = 3 cm = 30 mm

⇒ Height (H) = 5 cm = 50 mm

For each cone:

⇒ Radius (r) = 1 mm

⇒ Height (h) = 1 cm = 10 mm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder = πR²H

Volume of Cone = 1/3 × πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the given cylinder = π × (30)² × 50 = 45,000π mm³

⇒ Volume of one cone = 1/3 × π × (1)² × 10 = 10π/3 mm³

⇒ Number of cones formed = Total Volume of Cylinder ÷ Volume of One Cone

⇒ Number of cones = 45,000π ÷ (10π/3)

⇒ Number of cones = 45,000 × (3 / 10)

⇒ Number of cones = 4500 × 3 = 13,500

**∴ The correct answer is 13,500 cones.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Melting and Recasting of Solids

When a solid object is melted and recast into a different shape, the overall volume of the material remains constant. Total Initial Volume = Total Final Volume.

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume of a right circular cylinder is given by V = πr²h, where r is the base radius and h is the height.

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a right circular cone is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height: V = 1/3 × πr²h.

questions.question: Three traffic signals change at intervals of 48, 72 and 108 seconds respectively. They start changing simultaneously at 8:20:00 hours for the first time. At what time will they change again simultaneously?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

3 traffic signals change after every 48, 72 and 108 respectively.

**Concept Used:**

Lowest Common Multiple

**Calculation:**

The time of changing the 3 traffic lights simultaneously will be the LCM of 48, 72, and 108 as the first common multiple of the numbers. 

By Prime Factorisation we will take LCM of 48, 72 and 108 seconds. 

48 = 2⁴ × 3

72 = 2³ × 3²

108 = 2² × 3³

LCM ( 48, 72, 108) = 2⁴ × 3³ = 432 

Hence after 432 seconds, they will change simultancously. 

⇒ 432/60 minutes 

⇒ 7 minutes 12 seconds 

**∴ Lights will change at 8:20:00 + 7 minutes + 12 seconds = 8:27:12 hours**

questions.question: (1 - (1)/(n)) + (1 - (2)/(n)) + (1 - (3)/(n)) + up to n term will result as:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The series consists of **n terms**, where each term is of the form (1 − k/n).

Separate the **integer parts** and the **fractional parts**: (1 + 1 + ... n times) − (1/n + 2/n + ... + n/n).

Sum of n ones = n. Sum of fractions = (1/n) × [n(n + 1)/2] = (n + 1)/2.

Net result = n − (n + 1)/2 = (2n − n − 1)/2 = (n − 1)/2.

**∴ The correct answer is (n − 1)/2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The series is (1 − 1/n) + (1 − 2/n) + (1 − 3/n) + ... up to **n terms**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of the first n **natural numbers** (Σn) = n(n + 1)/2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8391f68532e54f5fa60d3399691dc6ffcc26d0e7cb114ea295eac72dd8952761.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let S = (1 − 1/n) + (1 − 2/n) + (1 − 3/n) + ... + (1 − n/n)

⇒ S = (1 + 1 + 1 + ... up to n terms) − (1/n + 2/n + 3/n + ... + n/n)

⇒ S = n − (1/n) × (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n)

⇒ S = n − (1/n) × [n(n + 1)/2]

⇒ S = n − (n + 1)/2

⇒ S = (2n − (n + 1))/2

⇒ S = (2n − n − 1)/2

⇒ S = (n − 1)/2

**∴ The correct answer is (n − 1)/2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n positive integers is given by the formula S = n(n + 1)/2.

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is constant. The sum of n terms is Sₙ = (n/2)[first term + last term].

General Term of the Series

The k-th term of the given series is Tₖ = (1 − k/n). For k = n, the term becomes (1 − n/n) = 0.</p
